analysis.file_name: Nomura - McElligott - SEA LEGS TEND TO TAKE SOME TIME - 6 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: Sea Legs Tend to Take Some Time
key_insights: Thursday 11/5 saw a disorderly unwind across momentum, trend and high-Sharpe trades in all assets and regions, after weeks of gradual de-grossing and stop-outs by leveraged and hedge fund accounts. NDX outperforms SPX by 2z on the open Friday but is still -4z over five days.
Mechanical deleveraging flows were very large: target vol control sold about $72B on the day and $117B over the past week, and leveraged ETFs had a -$48B end-of-day rebalance.

Crowded high-Sharpe positions were hit hard: the semis/energy barbell, AI enablers vs hyperscalers, short skew, short correlation and short gamma in equity vol, short bonds plus long commodities, and long carry and momentum/trend in risk premia.

McElligott names the likely pivot as the US midterm election result, read as a 'Blue Tsunami' for Democrats on an anti-AI platform. The note says it hit the IPO window, with frontier labs closing at much lower valuations and facing harder debt and equity raises for the expected capex spending.

The note says AI capex has been a main support for US nominal GDP over the past year or more, and that the AI enablers/bottlenecks were the year's winners. Tighter funding therefore adds weight to the economic and market left tail.
The jobs report was strong: NFP and average hourly earnings were hot and the unemployment rate fell. The December Fed hike is about 80% priced and cumulative pricing is about 50bps of hikes.

McElligott says he wrongly judged a true crash unlikely. His reasons were flat options skew, reduced VIX leveraged ETN assets and leveraged funds netting down. He expected a grinding 'spot down, vol down' selloff and a possible upside chase into year-end.

Positioning in AI was heavily one-sided before the drop: systematic equity positioning touched the 95th percentile within two weeks (vol control, CTA trend and risk parity combined), and leveraged ETF assets were at the 98th percentile last week.
Many holder types are long AI through index weights, beta or leverage: passive and mutual funds, multi-strategy and long-short funds, pensions, sovereigns, endowments, VC/PE and retail.

Customer activity is very quiet after the losses, which makes re-risking into year-end hard. Vol control flow is still live, and a move of more than 50bps either way would mean more deallocation selling.

For investors with cash and a good year, the note favours buying options premium to trade bounces. It still likes energy as a hiding place with upside because defensives have run so far. It also expects some to look at hyperscalers, where cutting capex could lead to a re-rating on higher free cash flow.

Shock backtests show choppy trading for the next couple of weeks to one month, then a cleaner path. Year-end P&L pressure and liquidation by slower-moving holders could cap early rallies until about the one-month turn.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers cutting capex ambitions could produce a bullish re-rating as free cash flow improves, and bounces can be traded with options by investors who have cash.
tension_points.bear_case: Harder funding for frontier labs threatens the capex trickle-down that supported nominal GDP and the AI enablers, and hot jobs data raise the odds of more Fed hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: More than 50bps index moves in either direction would trigger more vol control deallocation selling, and liquidation from slower-moving holders could continue until the roughly one-month turn.
